newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand injects funds to ailing property sector.
newsitem.headline: Thailand injects funds to ailing property sector.

text.p: The Thai government said it plans to loan between 20 billion and 70 billion baht ($800 million and $2.8 billion) to the ailing Thai property sector to help it out of a three-year slump.

Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan told reporters late on Wednesday that state-owned Government Savings Bank and the Government Housing Bank would jointly lend up to 20 billion baht of concessional mortgage loans to civil servants buying their first homes.
Amnuay said a quarter of the funds being lent by the two banks would be provided by the central bank which would charge only 0.1 percent annual interest rate for its fund.

The two state-owned banks, which would also issue bonds to raise funds for the special housing loans, would charge civil servants an interest rate of between eight and nine percent, compared with about 13 percent charged by private commercial banks.
Civil servants borrowing the funds would also be exempt from a property transaction tax.
Amnuay said the government also planned to set aside up to 50 billion baht for temporary state takeovers of private property projects facing financial problems.
He said the plan was not finalised because the central bank must still hold talks with commercial banks and finance companies on details of rescuing troubled property projects. He did not elaborate.
